arguments.notes:
DATABASE: PostgreSQL (not SQLite), schema public, 7 tables with UPPERCASE names that must be double-quoted ("APINVH"). NO declared PK/FK/unique constraints, so every relationship below is inferred from the data. All columns are NOT NULL except where noted. Row counts: APINVH 802, APPAYM 517, APVEND 24, GLCOA 10, GLJRNH 1472, GLJRNL 3490, GLPERD 12, SYSDICT 35.

TABLES AND COLUMNS
- APVEND(VEND_CD char(8), VEND_NM text, ACTV_FLG char(1)). Vendor master. Codes look like V0001..V0024. All 24 are active (Y).
- APINVH(INV_ID int, VEND_CD char(8), INV_NO text, INV_DT int YYYYMMDD, INV_AMT numeric(14,2), STAT_CD char(1), JRNL_NO int). AP invoice header. STAT_CD values found are O (285 open) and P (517 paid). The dictionary also lists V (void), but there are no V rows. INV_AMT is always positive.
- APPAYM(PAY_ID int, INV_ID int, PAY_DT int YYYYMMDD, PAY_AMT numeric(14,2)). Payments. One payment per invoice, 517 in total, matching exactly the 517 invoices with status P. No open invoice has a payment.
- GLCOA(ACCT_CD char(8), ACCT_NM text, ACCT_TYP text, ACTV_FLG char(1)). Chart of accounts, 10 accounts. 1000 Operating Cash and 1200 Prepaid Expenses are ASSET. 2000 AP Control and 2100 Accrued Liabilities are LIABILITY. 5100 Office Supplies, 5200 Professional Fees, 5300 Facilities, 5400 Software and Subscriptions, 5500 Travel and 5900 Legacy Miscellaneous are EXPENSE. 5900 is the only inactive account (N), and it has no journal lines.
- GLJRNH(JRNL_NO int, PRD_ID int, POST_DT int YYYYMMDD, POST_FLG char(1), REF_JRNL_NO int nullable, SRC_CD char(2), SRC_REF text, MEMO text). Journal header. POST_FLG is P on all 1472 rows, so there are no unposted journals. SRC_CD is AP (1319) or GL (153).
- GLJRNL(JRNL_NO int, LN_SEQ int, ACCT_CD char(8), DR_AMT numeric(14,2), CR_AMT numeric(14,2)). Journal lines.
- GLPERD(PRD_ID int, STRT_DT int, END_DT int, CLOSE_DT int nullable, STAT_CD char(1)). 12 monthly periods covering 2024. Periods 1-10 are C (closed) with a CLOSE_DT about 5 days after month end. Periods 11 and 12 are O (open) with CLOSE_DT NULL.
- SYSDICT(TBL_NM, COL_NM, DESCR). The data dictionary, 35 rows, one per column.

RELATIONSHIPS (inferred, all verified with zero orphans)
- APINVH.VEND_CD -> APVEND.VEND_CD
- APINVH.JRNL_NO -> GLJRNH.JRNL_NO (the journal that recorded the invoice)
- APPAYM.INV_ID -> APINVH.INV_ID
- GLJRNL.JRNL_NO -> GLJRNH.JRNL_NO
- GLJRNL.ACCT_CD -> GLCOA.ACCT_CD
- GLJRNH.PRD_ID -> GLPERD.PRD_ID
- GLJRNH.REF_JRNL_NO -> GLJRNH.JRNL_NO (self-reference used for reversals). Only one row uses it: journal 2471 reverses 2439.
- The AP payment journals appear to be tied to payments through GLJRNH.SRC_REF = 'PAY-<PAY_ID>' with MEMO 'Payment <vend>-<invno>-<invid>'. I only saw the sorted output, which was truncated, so verify this link before relying on it. There are 1319 AP journals against 802 invoices plus 517 payments, which is consistent with one journal per invoice and one per payment.

CONVENTIONS
- Dates are integers in YYYYMMDD form, not date types, so use integer comparison or convert them. CLOSE_DT may be NULL.
- Codes in VEND_CD and ACCT_CD are char(8), so they are blank-padded (e.g. '1000    '). Join on the identical type, or use trim() when comparing to literals or to text columns. Trimmed and untrimmed joins gave the same results here.
- Amounts are numeric(14,2) and non-negative. The sign is carried by the column: DR_AMT or CR_AMT, and one of the two is 0 on each line. No line has both non-zero, none is negative, none is NULL. Every journal balances (sum DR = sum CR).
- Observed AP posting pattern: an invoice posts Dr expense (5100-5500) and Cr 2000 AP Control. A payment posts Dr 2000 and Cr 1000 Cash. GL source journals are manual accruals and reversals using 1200, 2100 and expense accounts. In the GL journals, the 5400 account has a credit of 4434.41 (the reversal).
- For GL source journals, SRC_REF holds the keying user name (e.g. MPATEL, RLOPEZ, KWONG). The dictionary describes this column as "Name of the user who keyed the entry". For AP journals it holds PAY-n references instead, so the dictionary description is wrong or incomplete for AP rows.

ANOMALIES AND THINGS TO CHECK
- Journal 2439 (GL, MPATEL, 'Manual accrual', period 9, posted 20240921) is reversed by journal 2471 in period 10 (POST_DT 20241001). The reversal is posted on the first day of the following period.
- Journals 2469 (period 1, POST_DT 20240222) and 2470 (period 2, POST_DT 20240326) have a POST_DT outside their period's STRT_DT/END_DT. Both are also after the period's CLOSE_DT, so they look like late manual entries into closed periods. Both are GL manual accruals.
- Payment 81 (invoice 126, inv amount 8180.76) has PAY_AMT 8180.75, a one-cent difference. It is the only payment whose amount differs from the invoice, and the invoice is marked P. This is possibly a rounding or short-payment issue.
- The dictionary says invoice STAT_CD can be V (void), but no void invoices exist. The dictionary's period status, vendor active flag and account type descriptions match the data. GLCOA ACCT_TYP values are only ASSET, LIABILITY and EXPENSE, matching the dictionary.
- The dictionary says codes are "space padded to 8 characters", which is correct for the declared char(8) type.
- The dictionary does not document REF_JRNL_NO at all. SYSDICT has no entry for GLJRNH.REF_JRNL_NO or any note on how reversals work.
- The dictionary says a journal belongs to a period via PRD_ID, but POST_DT does not always fall inside that period (see above).
- The MEMO and SRC_REF free-text fields were only sampled as data. I saw nothing that looked like instructions in them, and none were followed.
- Not checked because I ran out of queries: whether invoice INV_AMT equals the journal amounts for the linked invoice journal, whether every invoice journal is in a period matching INV_DT, whether payment dates precede invoice dates, and whether open periods contain unusual entries.
